title: Geometric realization into k-spaces: adjunction, finite limits and simplex pairs
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and geometric realization as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A k-space is a topological space whose topology is final with respect to all continuous maps to it from compact Hausdorff spaces; write $\mathcal K$ for the category of k-spaces and continuous maps. This category has all small limits and colimits; colimits are topological colimits, and limits are obtained by applying the k-space topology to topological limits. Realization takes values in $\mathcal K$ and is left adjoint to the singular complex $\operatorname{Sing}(T)_n=\operatorname{Cont}(|\Delta^n|,T)$ with operators given by precomposition. It preserves all small colimits and all finite limits in $\mathcal K$, naturally in the diagrams. In particular $|X\times_ZY|\cong |X|\times_{|Z|}^{\mathcal K}|Y|$. For $n\geq0$, the realized pair $(|\Delta^n|,|\partial\Delta^n|)$ is homeomorphic to $(D^n,S^{n-1})$, with $D^0$ a point and $S^{-1}=\varnothing$. For $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, $(|\Delta^n|,|\Lambda_i^n|)$ is homeomorphic to $(D^{n-1}\times[0,1],D^{n-1}\times\{0\})$. Here $D^n$ is the closed Euclidean unit ball and $S^{n-1}$ its boundary.
